chunks: And as for what al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Zur'ah from Samaan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the waiting period ('iddah) of a female slave whose husband dies, and he said: one and a half months. This is a report in which the narrator may have erred in its transmission, because it is not impossible that he heard this ruling regarding a divorced female slave, since we have clarified that the waiting period of a divorced female slave, if she is among those who do not menstruate but is of an age where she could menstruate, is one and a half months. Thus, it became confused for him, and he narrated it regarding the one whose husband dies. On this basis, it does not contradict the previously mentioned reports.

key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period (period of time a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband before remarriage)
key_terms.وَهَمَ: Erred / made a mistake in transmission

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a female slave whose husband dies, and how is it reconciled with the ruling for a divorced slave?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of *ikhtilal* (narrative confusion) to resolve an apparent contradiction, suggesting that the narrator Sama'ah may have conflated the ruling for a divorced slave with that of a widow. This scholarly reconciliation preserves the consistency of the 'iddah period (one and a half months) for both categories under specific conditions, demonstrating the meticulous attention to detail in Shia hadith criticism.
